content.text:
**Recommendation: Sentry**, unless your app is mostly native mobile, in which case Bugsnag is the stronger pick.

I haven't checked current pricing, and these vendors change plans often, so confirm the numbers on each pricing page before you decide.

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core strength** | Error tracking plus performance tracing, session replay, profiling, logs, and cron monitoring in one platform | Focused, low-noise error grouping and a fast setup | Stability and release-health monitoring, strong mobile SDKs |
| **Language and SDK coverage** | Broadest; most frameworks have first-party SDKs | Broad for web and backend | Broad, with the best native iOS/Android support |
| **Source maps, releases, alerts** | Mature; deploy tracking, suspect commits, and integrations with GitHub, Slack, Jira, and PagerDuty | Solid | Solid; good release-stability views |
| **Pricing model** | Free tier, then usage-based plans; paid tiers usually include multiple users | Free tier, then per-event pricing | Free tier, then event-based plans; check whether seats are priced separately |
| **Self-hosting** | Open source, self-hostable | Hosted only | Hosted only |
| **Biggest drawback** | Breadth can mean more to configure and more to pay for as usage grows | Narrower product; less useful beyond error tracking | Weaker outside error monitoring; less of a general observability platform |

**Why Sentry for a 10-person team:**
- It covers the likely next needs (performance, replay, cron jobs) without adding a second vendor.
- It has the largest community, so most setup questions already have answers.
- Self-hosting is available if data residency becomes a concern.
- Its free tier is enough to evaluate it properly.

**When to pick something else:**
- **Bugsnag:** most of your code is in iOS or Android apps, and you care most about crash-free sessions and release health.
- **Rollbar:** you want error tracking and nothing else, and you want the simplest setup and the least noise.

**Before you commit:**
1. Estimate your monthly event volume. This drives cost on all three.
2. Check whether each plan charges per seat. For 10 people, this can change the answer.
3. Run a two-week trial of Sentry on your main service. Confirm that source maps, release tracking, and your alert channel (Slack, PagerDuty, etc.) work the way you need.

If you tell me your stack (languages, web vs. mobile, and rough event volume), I can narrow this to one choice.
